name: Risk parity allocation
heading: The Structural Opportunity: Harvesting Diversified Risk Premiums
caseLead: Risk parity allocates portfolio risk rather than capital across asset classes, reducing dependence on equities and seeking returns from several sources. The approach reflects differences in the volatility of stocks, bonds and commodities and may benefit from return diversification when growth, inflation and policy expectations affect these markets differently.
caseRest: Stocks and bonds can fall together during inflation shocks, reducing the diversification that risk parity relies on. Because the portfolio holds bonds with leverage, rising inflation and higher interest rates cause losses on its largest positions, as in 2022 when both asset classes recorded double-digit falls. A diversified allocation therefore does not protect against inflation shocks, and losses can be larger than those of a conventional portfolio over the same period.
figNote: Each card shows the change in the S&P 500 over the episode, measured at the daily close from the last high to the low in a fall. A fall of 20% or more is usually called a bear market, and the figure shows how much equity risk the portfolio carried when bonds either offset it or failed to.

events.title: US downgrade lifts Treasuries as shares fall
events.text: The US credit rating downgrade and the euro area debt crisis cut the S&P 500 by 17% between 22 July and 8 August 2011, while the 10-year Treasury yield fell to 2.3%. The strategy gained because the rise in bond prices outweighed the equity loss.

events.title: Fed taper signal pushes bond yields higher
events.text: The Federal Reserve's signal in May and June 2013 that it would slow bond purchases lifted the 10-year yield from 1.9% to 2.6% and cut the S&P 500 by 6%. The strategy lost because bonds, its largest holding after leverage, fell together with equities.

events.title: Covid sell-off hits bonds and equities together
events.text: The S&P 500 fell 34% from 19 February to 23 March 2020, and the 10-year yield rose from 0.5% to 1.3% in nine days as investors sold bonds for cash. The strategy lost because leveraged bond holdings no longer offset the fall in equities.

events.title: Inflation drives bonds and shares lower together
events.text: The S&P 500 fell 24% from January to 16 June 2022 as the Federal Reserve raised rates and the war in Ukraine lifted energy prices, while the 10-year yield rose from 1.5% to about 3.5%. The strategy lost because leveraged bonds fell with equities.

events.title: Equity sell-off is offset by a bond rally
events.text: The S&P 500 fell 8% between 16 July and 5 August 2024 as yen carry trades were closed, while the 10-year Treasury yield fell from 4.2% to 3.8%. The strategy gained because the bond rally offset the loss on equities.

events.title: Tariffs lift Treasury yields as shares fall
events.text: US tariff announcements cut the S&P 500 by 19% between 19 February and 8 April 2025, and lifted the 10-year yield by about 50 basis points in one week. Results were mixed because gold offset part of the loss on bonds and equities.

instrument: ETFs and futures covering equities, Treasuries, inflation-linked bonds, gold and commodities; rebalanced monthly
rules: Weights set so that each asset class contributes equal risk, using 60-day volatility; bond exposure raised with Treasury futures; leverage reduced when the correlation between stocks and bonds is above 0.4
costs: Estimated ETF bid-ask spreads, fund fees and financing costs deducted at each monthly rebalance
constructionTitle: Strategy construction, from equal risk weights to leverage limits

legs.purpose: Diversifies equity risk when growth slows
Adds bond exposure to balance risk across assets

entry: Rebalance when any asset class's risk share differs from its 25% target by more than 5 points
size: Set to a 9% annualised volatility target
exit: Positions reduced when an asset's 60-day volatility doubles
stop: Leverage removed if the portfolio falls 15% from its high
marketWatch: The correlation between equity and bond returns, inflation expectations and the path of central bank policy rates are key indicators. Rehyn watches inflation data and Treasury auctions because a positive correlation between stocks and bonds reduces the benefit of diversification. Upcoming trade policy decisions and energy price moves matter because they can raise inflation and push stocks and bonds down together.

favourable.heading: Stable low inflation
favourable.text: Low inflation favours the strategy because bonds then rise when growth slows, so they offset equity losses. From 2010 to 2019, US inflation averaged about 1.8% and the correlation between stocks and bonds was mostly negative, which supported the strategy.

favourable.heading: Falling yields during equity sell-offs
favourable.text: Falling yields during an equity sell-off favour the strategy because leveraged bonds gain by more than equities lose. In August 2011 and August 2024, the 10-year yield fell by about 60 and 40 basis points while equities fell.

favourable.heading: Commodity gains when inflation rises
favourable.text: Rising inflation expectations favour the strategy because the commodity and inflation-linked bond holdings gain when inflation exceeds forecasts. In 2021, the Bloomberg Commodity Index rose about 27% and US inflation-linked bonds gained about 6%.

adverse.heading: Stocks and bonds falling together
adverse.text: A positive correlation between stocks and bonds hurts the strategy because bonds stop offsetting equity losses, and leverage magnifies the fall. In 2022 the S&P 500 fell about 18% and long-dated Treasuries fell about 30%, so the portfolio lost on both of its largest positions.

adverse.heading: Sudden rise in interest rates
adverse.text: Rapid rate rises hurt the strategy because bond prices fall by more than their risk estimates suggest, and leverage magnifies the loss. In May and June 2013, the 10-year yield rose by about 70 basis points in six weeks, and long-dated Treasury ETFs fell by more than 10%.

adverse.heading: Forced deleveraging in a crisis
adverse.text: A rush for cash hurts the strategy because investors sell bonds and equities together, and funds reduce leverage at the same time. In March 2020, the 10-year yield rose by about 70 basis points in nine days during the equity sell-off.

infoHist: Historical results show the strategy's peak-to-trough drawdown during each event, measured from its value just before the event to its lowest point using the default backtest parameters above. Each event window runs from the last market high before the shock to the market low.
infoForward: Scenario results show the estimated profit or loss over the first month of each scenario. Rehyn's scenario engine projects moves in equity prices, Treasury yields, gold and commodity prices, which are then applied to the strategy's current holdings, including the leveraged bond position.
